config.text: Image 1 is a reference for the card, the paper, the two hot-foil layers, the photography and the vigour of the poses; generate a new design on the same card. The card: one tall narrow vertical menu card, proportion 10 by 21 centimetres, thick uncoated deep burgundy cotton paper, colour #560002, photographed flat from above on a pale warm grey linen cloth, soft even daylight, the whole card visible. The printing is only hot-foil stamping in two flat layers: the salmon in matte white foil underneath, the lamb in bright silver foil on top, opaque where they overlap. Each foil is a uniform solid area with crisp edges and a slight debossed relief; inner details are thin burgundy cut lines in the foil, with no gradients and no shading. The card carries no lettering. Drawing style: a medieval illuminated bestiary drawing, as in thirteenth-century English bestiaries and manuscript marginalia, translated into flat foil. Elongated, stylised animal bodies; the lamb's fleece drawn as rows of small tight spiral curls; the salmon's scales as a regular pattern of small crescents; fins and tails drawn like ornamental leaves; a few slender medieval vine tendrils ending in trefoil leaves. Confident outlines, decorative and precise, while the bodies keep the strong twisting energy of Image 1. The drawing avoids any Japanese woodblock character: no wave motifs, no ukiyo-e brushwork. Faces are calm and neutral: mouths closed, no teeth, a simple almond-shaped medieval eye, a serene gaze. Composition, same logic as Image 1: a dance of leaping lambs and jumping salmon scattered over the card, overlapping one another, with a few small eight-pointed stars. Density: dense. The figures fill the card edge to edge and touch or slightly run off the borders; very little burgundy shows. The dance has about twelve animals in total, half lambs, half salmon.
